summary: We developed SEAmon to help people explore coastal conditions and understand environmental changes around seaweed farming regions. Users can select a seaweed species and region on an interactive globe. Our analysis of NASA data examines long-term changes in sea surface temperature, rainfall, and wind, showing where conditions are changing, by how much, and whether those trends are statistically significant. Changing conditions can place seaweed under stress. SEAmon uses this context to help users explore possible links to problems such as ice-ice disease, which can damage seaweed crops. For the challenge (Be An Earth System Trend Detective!), our team also collected and analysed historical environmental data and tested whether trends are statistically significant. SEAmon aims to make environmental information easier for farmers, researchers, and communities to understand and identify areas that need closer monitoring and protect the livelihoods that depend on seaweed.
details:
• What exactly does it do?

SEAmon is a web app for exploring coastal conditions around seaweed farming regions. Users can choose a species and location on a 3D globe and explore sea temperature, salinity, and rainfall layers.

• How does it work?

The globe displays environmental map layers from NASA. Our data pipeline prepares regional records for charts and environmental assessments. Separate research scripts analyse historical NASA temperature and weather records, measuring how quickly conditions change and testing whether trends are statistically significant.

• What benefits does it have?

Changing conditions can stress seaweed and may contribute to conditions associated with ice-ice disease. SEAmon helps users investigate these changes and identify areas that need closer monitoring. It does not diagnose disease.

• What do you hope to achieve?

We want to make environmental data easier for farmers, researchers, and coastal communities to understand and use when planning monitoring.

• What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Website: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, and Parcel

Data and trend analysis: Python

Storage: Supabase/PostgreSQL

Web services: Cloudflare

Collaboration: GitHub

Design: Sketch, Adobe Illustrator

Runs in browser without additional sensors or special hardware
